meta.title: Good Word: show and movie recs from your friends
meta.description: A private shelf of shows and movies your friends vouch for. No algorithm, no strangers.

hero.headline: Take your friends' word for it.
hero.subhead: A private shelf of shows and movies your friends vouch for. No algorithm. No strangers. Just your people.
hero.phoneAlt: A group shelf for College crew showing four shows and movies with the friends who vouched for them.
hero.quote: ep 3 is where it gets you. trust me.

problem.headline: You asked the group chat what to watch.
problem.body: Three days later, one reply. It was a link to a trailer. Meanwhile the algorithm still thinks you want another true-crime documentary because you watched one in 2022.
problem.algorithmCaption: Because you watched Baking Showdown: Season 4
problem.friendQuote: ok you need to watch The Night Ferry. it's strange and perfect.

how.headline: Three things. That's the whole app.
how.step1Body: Search a title, tap once, add a note if you like. About ten seconds.
how.step1Alt: Putting in a good word for The Night Ferry, with the note “ep 3 is where it gets you”, visible to 2 groups and 11 people.
how.step2Title: It lands on your groups' shelves.
how.step2Body: College friends, the group chat, your book club. Each group keeps its own shelf.
how.step2Alt: Two shelves, College crew and The girls, each showing The Night Ferry.
how.step3Body: Filter by mood, length, and where it's streaming, and every pick still has a friend's name on it.
how.step3Alt: A shelf filtered to comedy, under 2 hours, on Netflix, showing three picks and who vouched for each.

groups.headline: Different friends, different taste.
groups.body: You'd trust your film friend on a slow Korean thriller and your sister on a comfort rewatch. Keep a separate shelf for each circle.

talk.headline: Finished it? Say so.
talk.body: Every title on your shelf has a conversation, just for that group. Mention a friend to pull them in. Mark spoilers so nobody gets ruined.
talk.phoneAlt: A conversation about The Night Ferry in College crew: Tess says she just finished episode 6 and mentions Priya, Mo's comment is covered as a spoiler, and the comment box says “Say something to College crew…”.
talk.note: Conversations stay inside the group. No one else can see them.

humans.headline: Humans only.
humans.lead1: Every pick has a name on it.
humans.rest1: If it's on the shelf, a friend put it there.
humans.rest2: Nothing is logged unless you choose to vouch for it.
humans.rest3: If none of your friends have vouched for a short horror movie yet, we'll just tell you.

isnt.label: What Good Word isn't
isnt.summary: Good Word has no star ratings, public profiles, followers, endless feeds, or reviews.

faq.headline: Questions
faq.a1: No. Groups are private and invite-only. Only people in a group can see its shelf and its conversations.
faq.a2: Shows and movies to start. Restaurants and “who's your plumber” may come later.
faq.q3: Do I have to log everything I watch?
faq.a3: No. Only what you'd recommend. It's a shelf of favorites, not a diary.
faq.q4: Can we talk about what we watched?
faq.a4: Yes. Every title has a conversation for your group, with mentions and spoiler covers.
faq.a5: Only behind the scenes, to match titles and fill in details. It never recommends anything on its own.
faq.a6: We're building it now. Coming soon.

closing.headline: Your friends already have great taste.
closing.subhead: Good Word makes sure none of it gets lost.

footer.madeBy: Made by people who ask their friends what to watch.

help.title: Help

faq.whatA: It's a show or movie you'd vouch for, with an optional note. It goes on the shelf of each group you pick, with your name on it.
faq.whoQ: Who can see my good words?
faq.whoA: Only members of the groups you share them with. The visibility line tells you who before you put one in. Nothing on Good Word is public.
faq.groupsQ: How do groups and invites work?
faq.groupsA: Anyone in a group can share its invite link. Whoever opens it can join after signing in. The owner can reset the link, which stops the old one working.
faq.leaveQ: How do I leave a group?
faq.leaveA: Open the group from your shelf, then choose Leave group at the bottom of its details. Your good words leave that shelf too.
faq.deleteQ: How do I delete my account?
faq.deleteA: Go to Settings, then Delete account. Your good words and comments are removed everywhere, and this can't be undone.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: Good Word is a small, private app for sharing what you'd watch with friends. This page says what we collect, why, who can see it, and how to delete it. We is Sydney Stubbs, who makes Good Word.
privacy.s1b: Your email address, so you can sign in. The name you choose, your region, and your timezone. The groups you start or join. Your good words and notes, your comments and mentions, and your email settings. Feedback you send us. Basic records of how the app is used, like when a good word is put in, kept on our own systems.
privacy.s2b: Only to run Good Word: to sign you in, show your good words to your groups, send the emails you've chosen, show where to watch in your region, and improve the app. We don't sell your data, show ads, or use it to recommend anything on our own.
privacy.s3b: Members of a group see that group's members, the good words shared into it, and its conversations. Nobody outside your groups can see any of it, and nothing on Good Word is public or indexed by search engines. Your email address is never shown to other people.
privacy.s4b: Supabase stores the app's data and handles sign-in. Vercel hosts the app. Resend sends our emails. Google handles sign-in if you choose Continue with Google. Title details and posters come from TMDB, with streaming data from JustWatch; they don't receive your personal data. There are no third-party analytics or advertising trackers.
privacy.s5b: We send sign-in links, and, if you leave them on, a weekly digest, mention emails, and a note when someone joins your group. Every email has a one-click unsubscribe, and you can change them any time in Settings. We don't track whether you open our emails.
privacy.s6b: We keep your data while you have an account. You can download a copy any time in Settings. When you delete your account, it's removed from the app straight away, and fully purged from our systems, including backups, within 30 days.
privacy.s7b: Good Word is for people 13 and older. We don't knowingly collect data from anyone younger; if you think we have, tell us and we'll delete it.
privacy.s8b: If this page changes in a way that matters, we'll tell you in the app or by email before it takes effect.
privacy.s9b: Questions or requests: use Send feedback in Help, or email sydneytstubbs@gmail.com.

terms.title: Terms
terms.intro: These terms are the agreement between you and Good Word (Sydney Stubbs, who makes it) when you use the app. By using Good Word, you agree to them.
terms.s1b: You need to be 13 or older. You're responsible for your account and for keeping access to your email address safe, since that's how you sign in.
terms.s2b: You own the good words, notes, and comments you share. You give Good Word permission to store them and show them to the members of the groups you share them with, which is what the app is for. Delete something, or your account, and that permission ends.
terms.s3b: Don't use Good Word to harass anyone, share anything illegal, impersonate someone, send spam, or try to get into groups, accounts, or data that aren't yours. Group owners can remove members, and we may suspend accounts that break these rules.
terms.s4b: Title details and posters come from TMDB, and where-to-watch data comes from JustWatch. They're provided as they are, and may be incomplete or out of date. Good Word isn't endorsed or certified by TMDB or JustWatch.
terms.s5b: Good Word is new and still changing. We work to keep it running and your data safe, but it's provided as it is, without guarantees that it will always be available or free of errors. As far as the law allows, we aren't liable for indirect losses from using it.
terms.s6b: You can delete your account any time in Settings. We may close accounts that break these terms, or end the service; if we end it, we'll tell you first and give you time to download your data.
terms.s7b: If these terms change in a way that matters, we'll tell you in the app or by email before the change takes effect.
terms.s8b: Questions: use Send feedback in Help, or email sydneytstubbs@gmail.com.
